3. A manufacturable candidate cartridge—and the optical/mechanical tradeoff
Contact construction

The candidate uses a hardened DIN 6325 16m6 × 60 mm pin, ground to 52 mm, with restored small end chamfers and measured radius. That is obtainable stock, but a catalogue dowel pin does not carry a rating for this custom impact contact.

The operating half-gap is 90–100 μm, set by ground stops and shims matched to the measured pin. A further 5 μm keeper allowance enters the catch calculation.

The following calculation puts the entire 10 kN screening load on one land, rather than assuming equal sharing:

Quantity	Calculated screen
Hertz contact full width	0.664 mm
Hertz peak pressure	2.396 GPa
Pin bending stress, 36 mm span	224 MPa
Pin bending deflection	14.4 μm
Remaining land-edge margin at ±1.5 mm total offset	0.138 mm

This is not a qualified bearing capacity. The near-edge Hertz approximation is especially limited; hardness, impact, subsurface damage and permanent set remain unmeasured.

A 1 mm optical land was rejected because it could not retain the represented contact during a catch. A 3 mm land also failed the contact-footprint screen. Increasing to 4 mm improved mechanical retention while making optical separation harder. That coupling prevents selecting a favorable gap and a favorable bearing width independently.

Real optical components and the installed-error problem

The proposed head uses a Kowa LM100FC24M 100 mm lens and Basler a2A4504-59g10m camera. The manufacturer documentation supplies the relevant lens family and camera geometry; it does not supply an installed 20 μm gap-error bound. The Kowa manufacturer page was out of stock when retrieved. A separate supplier advertised a lead time, which is not a confirmed procurement.
